Below is a practical, step‑by‑step guide you can follow (or adapt) to build a modern, production‑ready front‑end for your e‑commerce site. I’ll cover the whole pipeline – from choosing a framework to deploying the finished product – and sprinkle in code snippets, libraries, and best‑practice links so you can jump straight into implementation. --- ## 1️⃣ Pick Your Tech Stack | Option | Why it’s good for e‑commerce | Typical tech | |--------|-----------------------------|--------------| | **React + Vite** | Fast dev server, component reusability, huge ecosystem | React, Vite, TypeScript | | **Vue 3 + Vite** | Simpler learning curve, excellent single‑file components | Vue 3, Vite, TypeScript | | **SvelteKit** | Zero‑runtime overhead, built‑in routing & SSR | SvelteKit, TypeScript | | **Next.js (React)** | Built‑in SSR/SSG, API routes, image optimization | Next.js, React, TypeScript | > **Recommendation:** If you’re already comfortable with JavaScript, start with **React + Vite**. It gives you the flexibility of a SPA while still allowing you to add SSR later if you need SEO or faster first paint. --- ## 2️⃣ Project Skeleton ```bash # Create a new Vite + React + TS project npm create vite@latest ecommerce-frontend --template react-ts cd ecommerce-frontend # Install core dependencies npm i axios react-router-dom @tanstack/react-query npm i -D eslint prettier eslint-plugin-react eslint-config-prettier ``` ### Folder Layout ``` src/ ├─ assets/ # images, icons, fonts ├─ components/ # reusable UI pieces (Button, Card, Modal) ├─ pages/ # route‑specific components (Home, ProductDetail, Cart) ├─ hooks/ # custom hooks (useCart, useAuth) ├─ context/ # React Contexts (AuthContext, CartContext) ├─ services/ # API wrappers (productService.ts, authService.ts) ├─ styles/ # global CSS / SCSS / Tailwind config └─ utils/ # helpers (formatPrice, debounce) public/ ├─ index.html └─ favicon.ico ``` --- ## 3️⃣ Core Features & Implementation | Feature | Key Libraries | Code Snippet | |---------|---------------|--------------| | **Routing** | `react-router-dom` | ```tsx
import { BrowserRouter, Routes, Route } from 'react-router-dom';

test('renders product title', () => { render(); expect(screen.getByText(/Laptop/i)).toBeInTheDocument(); });``` | --- ## 4️⃣ Example Flow: Adding a Product to Cart ```tsx // src/context/CartContext.tsx export const CartContext = createContext(defaultValue); export const CartProvider: FC<{ children: ReactNode }> = ({ children }) => { const [cart, dispatch] = useReducer(cartReducer, []); return {children}; }; // src/hooks/useCart.ts export const useCart = () => useContext(CartContext); // src/pages/ProductDetail.tsx const ProductDetail = () => { const { id } = useParams(); const { data: product, isLoading } = useQuery(['product', id], () => fetchProduct(id)); const { dispatch } = useCart(); const addToCart = () => dispatch({ type: 'ADD_ITEM', payload: { productId: product.id, quantity: 1 } }); if (isLoading) return ; return (

{product.title}

); }; ``` --- ## 5️⃣ Performance & SEO | Technique | How to Implement | |-----------|------------------| | **Code Splitting** | Use dynamic imports (`React.lazy`) for heavy components. | | **SSR/SSG** | Switch to Next.js or use Vite’s SSR plugin. | | **Lazy Load Images** | `` or IntersectionObserver. | | **Critical CSS** | Extract critical CSS via `critical` npm package. | | **PWA** | Add a service worker (`vite-plugin-pwa`). | --- ## 6️⃣ Deployment Pipeline | Step | Tool | Notes | |------|------|-------| | **CI/CD** | GitHub Actions | Automate lint, test, build, deploy. | | **Hosting** | Vercel (for Next.js) or Netlify | Both support edge functions, instant rollbacks. | | **CDN** | Cloudflare Workers | Cache static assets globally. | | **Monitoring** | Sentry + LogRocket | Capture runtime errors and user sessions. | Example GitHub Action: ```yaml name: CI/CD on: push: branches: [main] jobs: build-deploy: runs-on: ubuntu-latest steps: - uses: actions/checkout@v3 - uses: actions/setup-node@v3 with: node-version: '20' - run: npm ci - run: npm run lint - run: npm run test - run: npm run build - uses: vercel/action@v1 with: vercel-token: ${{ secrets.VERCEL_TOKEN }} vercel-org-id: ${{ secrets.VERCEL_ORG_ID }} vercel-project-id: ${{ secrets.VERCEL_PROJECT_ID }} ``` --- ## 7️⃣ Resources & Further Reading | Topic | Link | |-------|------| | **React + Vite Starter** | https://vitejs.dev/guide/#scaffolding-your-first-vite-project | | **React Query Docs** | https://react-query.tanstack.com/overview | | **TailwindCSS Setup** | https://tailwindcss.com/docs/guides/vite | | **Stripe Checkout** | https://stripe.com/docs/payments/integration-builder | | **Accessibility Checklist** | https://www.w3.org/WAI/standards-guidelines/wcag/checklist | | **Performance Budgeting** | https://web.dev/performance-budget/ | | **Vercel Deployment** | https://vercel.com/docs/platform/deployments | --- ## TL;DR Checklist 1. Scaffold with Vite + React + TS. 2. Add routing, state, and data fetching layers. 3. Build reusable UI components (Button, Card, Modal). 4. Wire up product listing → detail → cart → checkout flows. 5. Integrate Stripe for payments. 6. Optimize images, lazy load, split code. 7. Set up CI/CD with GitHub Actions → Vercel. 8. Monitor with Sentry + LogRocket. Happy coding! 🚀 If you hit a specific roadblock (e.g., “how do I persist cart across sessions?” or “how do I protect admin routes?”), just let me know and I’ll dive deeper.
